newsitem.title: UK: BT to face investor pressure over MCI - papers.
newsitem.headline: BT to face investor pressure over MCI - papers.

text.p: Institutional investors have warned British Telecommunications Plc that they will block its $24 billion merger with MCI Communications Corp. unless the deal is renegotiated, British newspapers said Sunday.
The pressure from shareholders follows a profit warning Thursday from MCI, America's second biggest long-distance carrier.
Investors are concerned not only about BT paying too much for the deal but that the drain on the company's cash flow will dampen prospects for dividend growth.
The Sunday Times also said investors will be pushing BT to renegotiate the deal. The rationale for the merger remains but the British company was likely to take a closer look at the costs involved.

BT has set up a special task force and is prepared to send its own personnel into senior positions at MCI to scrutinise its finances and to find out how losses ran out of control, the Independent on Sunday said.

The Sunday Telegraph said two of MCI's most senior managers were expected to come under pressure to resign as a result of the losses -- Doug Maine, MCI's finance director and Tim Price, head of telecommunications business.

Traders wiped out over 2 billion pounds ($3.4 billion) of BT's market value Friday following MCI's warning late Thursday that losses due to heavy investments in local telephone markets would be more than twice what was forecast this year.
MCI said those losses could reach $800 million - and could be even higher next year.
